**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/23 (Tue) 06:30
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Release and Reclaim Religious Recovery Group has a team of facilitators who are helping professionals with lived experience of religious trauma.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Dr. Marlene Winell is the founder of Journey Free and a leading expert on Religious Trauma Syndrome (RTS).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Christine Chenitz has a master’s degree in Social Work and currently has a psychotherapy practice where she works with those who have experienced trauma of various types including religious and spiritual trauma and adverse religious experiences.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Janice Selbie is a Registered Professional Counsellor, born and raised in a Canadian evangelical Christian home, who experienced tragedies that prompted her to research other religions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Coco Owen is a licensed psychologist in Los Angeles who grew up in the Seventh-day Adventist Church.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Kevin Davison recalls an early Southern Illinois Pentecostal church where he first spoke in tongues after a laying on of hands in the children’s church basement.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Chase Marks is a former Jehovah's Witness who faced the reality of losing his family, friends, community, worldview, and sense of self after leaving the religion.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The group leads discussions and provides support on Zoom conference calls twice a month.
- [USER] Janelle felt empowered by being able to encourage others in the group and appreciated having people ready to listen and support her.
- [USER] Drew noted that there is great safety in exploring issues related to religious trauma with others who have shared similar experiences, praising Marlene's skills.
- [USER] Tracey expressed the importance of having people who understand her struggles and the feeling of being there for others in the group.
- [USER] Frank described his journey to reclaim his life from religious burdens and praised Marlene's clinical skills and the value of her book, "Leaving the Fold."
- [USER] Anne emphasized the importance of the group in her recovery from fundamentalism and recommended it to anyone questioning or leaving their faith.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Release and Reclaim Religious Recovery Group is a private, online support group that helps members release old, toxic beliefs and reclaim their lives.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The group is led by Dr. Marlene Winell, who has 30 years of experience in human services.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Participants in the group come from various backgrounds, including Christian fundamentalism, Pentecostalism, Islamic faith, Catholicism, and Mormonism.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The group offers confidential support, discussion, and twice-monthly Zoom conference calls
